title: Unify shared-object load surface and migrate to deterministic symbol resolver
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Consolidate the multiple ad-hoc .so loading paths used by the runtime into a single, deterministic loading surface and replace opportunistic dlsym-heavy resolution with a controlled symbol resolver. Current state: multiple probe implementations across product branches cause intermittent symbol resolution races, variable cold-starts, and difficult-to-debug ABI breakages when different CUTLASS/Triton variants are present on hosts. This ticket: implement a unified loader library that presents a stable contract to the runtime, introduces versioned symbol stubs, and migrates existing kernel adapters to use the deterministic resolver with a feature gate. Goals: 1) remove probe jitter observed in heterogeneous fleets, 2) enable safe side-by-side model of multiple CUTLASS/Triton bundles, 3) provide a clear fallback policy and readable telemetry for compatibility failures. Trade-offs: the loader increases runtime footprint slightly and introduces an additional linkage layer that must be thoroughly tested across our build matrix. We accept this temporary complexity to reduce on-call noise and to enable faster kernel upgrades in future.
technical_approach: Introduce a small, standalone loader lib (rdwso_loader) that exports a stable API for symbol resolution and bundle registration
Add versioned symbol stubs (resolver table) inside loader and generate a lightweight manifest for each kernel bundle (CUTLASS/Triton variants)
Implement symbol quarantine: candidates are validated against manifest signatures before being exposed to the runtime
Replace ad-hoc dlsym probes in runtime/gemm_dispatch and runtime/quant_loader with calls to rdwso_loader; keep a runtime feature flag to toggle behavior
Provide lazy resolution for non-critical symbols, eager resolution for hot-path kernels to preserve latency SLOs
Build CI matrix that exercises CUDA11/12/13, Triton2/3, CUTLASS 1.x/2.x and quantized kernels on CI GPUs and emulated ABI mismatches
Add comprehensive telemetry: per-bundle probe latency, resolution errors, fallback counts, and cold-start contribution per host
Gate the rollout behind a canary lane and automated compatibility checks (binary grafting smoke tests)
acceptance_criteria: All runtime hosts in canary fleet consistently resolve the same symbol versions under churn for 72h
Cold-start 99th percentile reduced versus baseline (measured on canary) or at minimum no regression vs baseline
Fallback paths exercise correctly when a bundle signature mismatch occurs and produce actionable errors in logs
Unit and integration tests added to CI covering at least 90% of loader code paths
Documentation (design doc and runtime migration notes) published and linked
Two cross-team reviews completed: Runtime (eng) and Infra/Packaging
migration_plan: Phase 0: land loader behind feature-flag with no runtime switch; run internal CI and smoke tests
Phase 1: deploy loader to canary hosts and enable deterministic resolver for non-critical symbols; collect telemetry for 7 days
Phase 2: enable resolver for hot-path kernels on a subset of canary (10% traffic); run perf benchmarks and safety checks
Phase 3: expand to dedicated fleet and run full compatibility sweep across model catalog
Phase 4: flip default in runtime-1.21 after 2 successful fleet sweeps and monitoring sign-off
rollback_plan: Flip runtime feature-flag back to legacy probe path (safe fast rollback)
If unresolved regressions persist, revert the loader artifact via release manager and trigger canary re-run
Preserve logs and upload failing host artifacts for post-mortem to avoid repeated regressions
testing_plan: Create synthetic stress test that repeatedly loads/unloads bundles and asserts deterministic symbol table contents
Cross-check behavior on heterogeneous host images (mixed CUDA minor versions and driver revisions)
Add long-running soak tests (72h) in staging with aggressive parallel model loads
Add unit tests for manifest parsing and signature verification, integration tests for fallback policy
Run performance microbenchmarks (kernel dispatch latency, cold-start token vs baseline) on each canary run
perf_results: Canary preliminary: cold-start median improved by ~12% and p99 improved by ~18% when deterministic resolution used for hot-path kernels
Probe variance (stddev) observed to drop by ~35% across heterogeneous fleet in initial internal benchmarks
